- conda-forge
channel_targets:
- conda-forge main
docker_image:
- quay.io/condaforge/linux-anvil-x86_64:alma10
python_min:
- '3.11'

about.description:

powering conda's resolution process since its inception, historically
known as the classic solver (classic remains available as an alias).
It is packaged separately to benefit from the configurability of the
conda plugin system.

name: conda-pycosat-solver
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "0.1.0"

package:
  name: conda-pycosat-solver
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  # stable, checksummed archive uploaded by .github/workflows/upload.yml,
  # rather than GitHub's own auto-generated (and historically not
  # format-stable) archive link
  url: https://github.com/conda/conda-pycosat-solver/releases/download/${{ version }}/conda-pycosat-solver-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: ac103446d6f374a54f1427bdc364fc0755350242a8f3a106e7e879d2a463c8ec
  target_directory: src/

build:
  number: 0
  noarch: python
  script:
    env:
      SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION: ${{ version }}
    content: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install src/ -vv

requirements:
  host:
    - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    - pip
    - hatchling >=1.12.2
    - hatch-vcs >=0.2.0
  run:
    - boltons >=23.0.0
    - frozendict >=2.4.2
    - packaging >=26.3
    - pycosat >=0.6.3
    - python >=${{ python_min }}
    - tqdm >=4
  run_constraints:
    # Technically a run dependency (imported at runtime), but conda already
    # bundles conda-pycosat-solver by default, so a hard `run` dependency
    # here would create a dependency cycle that complicates migrations.
    - conda >=23.7.3

tests:
  # rattler-build doesn't support `requirements` in `python` block,
  # so copy the same script block twice to test oldest and newest python.
  # xref https://github.com/conda-forge/staged-recipes/pull/34939
  # we need this because conda is a soft-dependency in run-constraints only
  # to avoid dependency cycles with conda (which depends on this package).
  - script:
      - python -c "import conda_pycosat_solver"
      - python -m pip check
      - conda create -c conda-forge -n test --dry-run scipy --solver=pycosat
      - conda create -c conda-forge -n test --dry-run scipy --solver=classic
    requirements:
      run:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - conda
        - pip
  - script:
      - python -c "import conda_pycosat_solver"
      - python -m pip check
      - conda create -c conda-forge -n test --dry-run scipy --solver=pycosat
      - conda create -c conda-forge -n test --dry-run scipy --solver=classic
    requirements:
      run:
        - python
        - conda
        - pip

about:
  license: BSD-3-Clause
  license_file: src/LICENSE
  summary: The pycosat solver used in conda, also available as classic
  description: |
    conda-pycosat-solver provides the pycosat-based SAT solver that has been
    powering conda's resolution process since its inception, historically
    known as the classic solver (classic remains available as an alias).
    It is packaged separately to benefit from the configurability of the
    conda plugin system.
  homepage: https://github.com/conda/conda-pycosat-solver
  repository: https://github.com/conda/conda-pycosat-solver
  documentation: https://conda.github.io/conda-pycosat-solver/

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - jaimergp
    - jezdez
    - kenodegard
